snapshot.descriptionShort: Snapshot every datastore in the cluster at one instant
snapshot.description: Point-in-time snapshots of the whole cluster. One crash-consistent instant across every rbd-backed datastore the cluster owns, taken through Ceph's group snapshot: nothing stops and the cluster never notices. Local-backend datastores have no block-level group primitive, so they fall outside the instant and are reported as such. The instant is crash-consistent, not application-consistent: if you need a specific write to be IN the snapshot, sync it first.

create.description: Snapshot every rbd-backed datastore in the cluster at ONE instant. Nothing is stopped. Any local-backend datastore in the cluster is listed as outside the instant: it is not part of the snapshot. The instant is crash-consistent, not application-consistent: if you need a specific write to be IN the snapshot, sync it first.

prune.descriptionShort: Sweep stale leftovers from the local config file
prune.description: Remove dead weight from the local config file at ~/.config/rediacc/<config>.json. Three buckets are cleaned, all pure-local (no SSH/renet calls): (1) ACME cert-cache entries whose anchor GUID/repo/machine is no longer in the active config; (2) archived repositories whose grace period has expired (default 7 days, see defaults.pruneGraceDays); (3) dangling cross-references (machine→strategy, strategy→repo). Resources still in use, credentials, storage tokens, and known-hosts are never touched. Default behavior is to apply changes; pass --dry-run to preview only.
prune.dryRunOption: Preview what would be removed without modifying the config file. Mirrors the default-off semantics of the other prune commands.
prune.certsOnlyOption: Restrict to the ACME cert-cache bucket. Skips archive purging and cross-reference cleanup. Mutually exclusive with --archives-only and --refs-only.
prune.archivesOnlyOption: Restrict to expired-archive purging. Skips cert-cache and cross-reference cleanup. Mutually exclusive with --certs-only and --refs-only.
prune.refsOnlyOption: Restrict to dangling cross-references (machine→strategy, strategy→repo excludes/includes). Skips cert-cache and archives. Mutually exclusive with --certs-only and --archives-only.
prune.purgeArchivedOption: Drop ALL archived repositories regardless of age, not just those past grace. Equivalent to running 'rdc repo admin archive purge' for every archived repo. Use only when you're sure you don't need any of the stashed credentials for restore.
prune.graceDaysOption: Override the archive grace window (in days) for this invocation. Falls back to defaults.pruneGraceDays in the config, then to 7 if neither is set.

prune.description: Remove orphaned datastore resources and stale snapshots from a machine. The base run cleans renet-internal datastore artifacts (BTRFS subvolumes, lock files, tmpfiles). The optional flags below enable progressively narrower repo cleanups: --orphaned-repos uses the local CLI config as the only signal, while --prune-unknown additionally consults the renet .interim/state mirror so legitimate forks created by other tools survive even when missing from your local config. Both deletion paths run a mount-safety preflight; pass --force-delete-mounted to override.

prune.dryRunOption: Show what would be removed without making changes
prune.startingDatastore: Scanning for orphaned datastore resources on {{machine}}...
prune.orphanedReposOption: Delete every repo image on the machine that is not in your local CLI config. Coarse — also removes forks created by other tools that have no local config entry, even when their renet mirror correctly identifies them as forks. Use --prune-unknown for the narrower behavior that respects the mirror.
prune.pruneUnknownOption: Delete only repos the renet .interim/state mirror cannot classify (not in local config AND no fork-marked mirror). Strictly narrower than --orphaned-repos: forks-without-config are preserved when the mirror identifies them. Pre-mirror legacy orphans and stale grands whose config entry was deleted both fall in this bucket.
prune.forceDeleteMountedOption: Override the mount-safety preflight and delete repos even if they are currently mounted or have running Docker containers. Distinct from --force (which only overrides the archive grace period). Applies to both --orphaned-repos and --prune-unknown.

Proxy routes take ~3s to become active after deploy. Prints the URL pattern for HTTP-exposed services (rediacc.service_port label) on completion. First deploy and forks are mounted automatically. CRIU checkpoint restore is auto-detected; use --skip-checkpoint to force fresh start. Use --all --machine <m> to deploy every repository on a machine.

up.checkpointOption: Restore CRIU checkpoint on start (resume processes from saved memory state)
up.allOption: Deploy every repository whose home is --machine (batch form)

down.description: Stop repository Docker containers (runs Rediaccfile down via renet compose). The machine is derived from the ref placement. Does NOT unmount the encrypted volume -- the repo stays mounted and can be restarted with 'repo up'. Use --unmount to also close the LUKS container after stopping (folds the retired 'repo unmount'). Use --checkpoint to save CRIU process state before stopping (next 'repo up' auto-restores). Use --all --machine <m> to stop every repository on a machine.

down.checkpointOption: Create CRIU checkpoint before stopping (save process memory state for later restore via 'repo up')

A mounted or running target is refused unless --force, which cleanly quiesces it first. Without --resolve it is a whole-image take-theirs (the target becomes the source); with --resolve ours|theirs it is a per-file three-way merge against the common ancestor, taking each side's unique changes and resolving two-sided conflicts per the flag.

fork.description: Create a CoW (Copy-on-Write) fork of a repository. FORK IS NEAR-INSTANT AND CONSTANT-TIME regardless of repo size, BTRFS reflink clones the underlying image so a 100 GB repo and a 1 GB repo fork in the same ~seconds. The fork gets a NEW GUID, networkId, IP range, and auto-route domain ({service}-fork-{tag}.{repo}.{machine}.{baseDomain}) and is a fully independent copy. Online forking is supported, the parent can remain running. Fork inherits the parent's encryption credentials automatically. Use --checkpoint to capture CRIU process state before forking, the fork will auto-restore on first 'repo up' (in-memory state preserved). CROSS-MACHINE FORK: fork locally first, then transfer: (1) rdc repo fork <parent-ref> --tag <name>, (2) rdc repo push <fork-ref> --to <target-machine>, (3) rdc backup restore <fork-ref> --as <fork-name> -m <target-machine> --up. WARNING: do NOT use "repo push" alone to fork, it creates a raw copy with the SAME GUID (not an independent fork). Always fork first to get a new identity. Auto-routes use the repo name, so each fork gets a unique domain automatically.
fork.descriptionShort: Near-instant CoW fork of a repository (new GUID, networkId, IP range)

replicate.descriptionShort: Instant read replicas from datastore forks
replicate.description: Create N read replicas of a repository in seconds, regardless of database size. Takes ONE datastore snapshot, then makes N constant-time fork-attaches (copy-on-write, throwaway local writes) spread across the cluster's nodes, and applies a generated overlay: one pinned PersistentVolume per replica, a StatefulSet, and two Services ({repo}-rw to the primary, {repo}-ro across the replicas). Replicas are POINT-IN-TIME copies: no replication stream, no read-your-writes; each replica runs one crash-recovery pass before serving. Refresh them with 'repo replicate refresh'. Replica sets are managed state: see 'repo replicate status' and remove with 'repo replicate remove'.

replicate.imageOption: Engine image the replicas run (same engine as the primary)
replicate.pvcOption: Volume name the engine mounts as its data dir (default: data)
replicate.primaryAppOption: The primary pod's 'app' label value the -rw Service targets (default: the repo name)
replicate.headlessOption: Make the -ro Service headless: DNS returns every replica pod IP for driver-side balancing (long-lived DB connections skew a normal Service's per-connection balancing)
replicate.refreshOption: Intended refresh interval recorded on the set (e.g. 1h); run 'repo replicate refresh' to roll it

remove.description: Remove a replica set: delete its generated k8s objects (label-scoped), discard its fork datastores, drop its snapshot, and forget the state. Infra steps are best-effort so removal converges even on a partially-gone cluster.

refresh.descriptionShort: Roll replicas onto a fresh snapshot
refresh.description: Roll every replica onto a fresh point-in-time snapshot, ONE at a time: bounce the replica pod, discard and re-fork its datastore under the same path, and let readiness re-admit it. N-1 replicas keep serving throughout.

canary.descriptionShort: Canary release: weighted traffic split on shared data
canary.description: Run a NEW image next to the stable one and split live traffic between them by percentage (release ladder rung 2). Creates one canary Deployment + Service on the SAME live data (no fork: canary users on forked data would read stale data and write into a doomed copy) and tells the Rediacc proxy to route the given percent of the stable hostname's traffic to it. Weight 0 keeps the canary dark; weight 100 is the blue/green flip. Before every canary change, an automatic group snapshot of the cluster's datastores is taken (release ladder rung 0) as the universal undo. Schema compatibility between the two versions (expand-contract) is the application's responsibility. For schema-BREAKING releases, use blue/green instead: fork the repo (instant, includes data), point the fork's Service here with weight 100, and roll back by restarting the untouched parent; writes made after the flip exist only in the new copy, so the rollback window is a policy decision.

canary.portOption: Port the app serves on (must match the stable Service)
canary.weightOption: Percent of traffic routed to the canary (integer 0-100; 0 = dark, 100 = full flip)
canary.serviceOption: Stable Service to split traffic with (default: the repo name)

weight.description: Change the percent of traffic routed to a canary. Takes a fresh release-undo group snapshot first, then re-applies the overlay; the proxy picks up the new split on its refresh tick. Weight 100 sends all traffic to the new version (the blue/green flip).

A group snapshot of the cluster's datastores is taken first, as the undo.

template.description: Manage and apply deployment templates (writes docker-compose.yml, Rediaccfile, and additional files). Rediaccfile must use 'renet compose' (not 'docker compose'). Restart policies are safe (auto-managed by renet watchdog). Renet auto-injects network_mode:host, CRIU capabilities, and rediacc labels. Dangerous settings (privileged, pid:host) are blocked. Use 'list' to see available built-in templates, 'apply' to deploy one to a repository

list.description: List all embedded deployment templates shipped with the CLI

apply.description: Apply a template to a repository. Use a built-in template name (e.g. app-postgres) or --file for a custom JSON template. Rediaccfile lifecycle: up() starts containers (pull images, generate configs here), down() stops. Minimal Rediaccfile: up() { renet compose -- pull; renet compose -- up -d; } down() { renet compose -- down; }. IMPORTANT: Rediaccfile MUST use 'renet compose': 'docker compose' is rejected. ENV VARS: two levels: (a) Rediaccfile shell: ${SVCNAME_IP} (e.g. APP_IP), ${REDIACC_WORKING_DIR}, ${REDIACC_NETWORK_ID}. (b) Inside containers: renet auto-injects SERVICE_IP and REDIACC_NETWORK_ID env vars. eBPF bind rewriting handles IP isolation transparently, so apps can bind to 0.0.0.0 and the kernel rewrites it to the correct loopback IP. Health checks can use localhost. network_mode:host is injected and ports: are ignored. STORAGE: Both ${REDIACC_WORKING_DIR}/... bind mounts and Docker named volumes are safe: Docker data-root is inside the encrypted LUKS mount. RESTART POLICY: Restart policies are safe: renet auto-strips them for CRIU compatibility and the watchdog handles recovery. Compose: do NOT add network_mode or rediacc.* labels (renet injects them). Multi-project: place each sub-project in its own subdirectory with its own Rediaccfile: renet auto-discovers and runs them in order. HTTPS routing: (A) Auto-route (fork-friendly, recommended): do NOT add traefik.enable. Renet auto-generates https://{serviceName}.{repoName}.{machineName}.{baseDomain}. Add rediacc.service_port=<port> label for non-80 ports. Each fork gets a unique domain. (B) Traefik labels (custom domain, NOT fork-friendly): traefik.enable=true, traefik.http.routers.<n>.rule=Host(`domain`), traefik.http.routers.<n>.entrypoints=websecure,websecure-v6, traefik.http.routers.<n>.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt, traefik.http.services.<n>.loadbalancer.server.port=<port>. For TCP/UDP: rediacc.tcp_ports=3306 / rediacc.udp_ports=53

help.keyConcepts:
Key Concepts:

  Architecture
    • Each repository = isolated Docker environment (own daemon, loopback IP range, encrypted LUKS storage)
    • Use renet compose (never raw docker compose) — auto-injects network_mode:host and rediacc.* labels
    • Storage: bind-mount to ${REDIACC_WORKING_DIR}/... — never Docker named volumes (excluded from forks/backups)
    • eBPF bind rewriting handles IP isolation: apps bind to 0.0.0.0 and the kernel rewrites to the correct loopback IP

  Routing
    • Auto-route (fork-friendly): https://{service}.{repo}.{machine}.{baseDomain}
    • Custom domain: Traefik labels (traefik.enable=true) — not fork-friendly
    • rediacc.service_port label for non-80 ports. Routes activate ~3s after deploy
    • HTTPS: automatic Let's Encrypt wildcard certs via Cloudflare DNS-01, which requires --cf-dns-token configured via 'rdc machine infra set'. Without it, HTTP works but HTTPS certs are not provisioned
    • Grand repos get *.{repo}.{machine}.{baseDomain} — provisioned automatically by Traefik on first repo up
    • Forks reuse the parent repo's wildcard cert (already provisioned, zero rate limit impact)

  Environment Variables
    • Rediaccfile shell: ${SVCNAME_IP}, ${REDIACC_WORKING_DIR}, ${REDIACC_NETWORK_ID}
    • Inside containers: SERVICE_IP, REDIACC_NETWORK_ID (auto-injected by renet)

  Forking
    • rdc repo fork <parent-ref> --tag <tag>: instant CoW clone with a new GUID, networkId, IP range, auto-route domain
    • Parent stays running (online forking). Cross-machine: fork locally, then rdc repo push <ref> --to <machine>
    • Config entry persists after repo delete (the repo may exist on other machines)
help.agentMode:
Agent Mode
    • Fork-only: create a fork before making changes to any repository
    • Grand (non-fork) repositories are read-only for agents
    • Workflow: repo fork <repo> --tag <tag> -> repo up <repo>:<tag> -> term connect <repo>:<tag>
    • A repository ref (repo[:tag]) derives its own machine, so -m is not needed
    • JSON output is automatic: all commands return { success, data, errors, metrics }
    • Always parse full JSON, never use tail/head/grep on JSON output
    • Use filter flags (e.g. --repositories, --containers) to reduce response size

machine.keyConcepts:
Key Concepts:

  Query Filters
    • rdc machine status <name> returns all sections by default
    • Use --system, --repositories, --containers, --services, --network, --block-devices to filter
    • JSON output enriches containers with: repository (resolved name), domain, autoRoute

  Health & Monitoring
    • machine health exits with: 0=healthy, 1=warning, 2=error — use for CI/CD gates
    • machine status <name> --containers --health-check exits 2 if any container is unhealthy
    • machine status <name> --services --stability-check exits 2 if any service is failed, restarting, or has >3 restarts
    • machine prune removes orphaned loopback IPs and systemd units from deleted repos

  Datastore Structure (/mnt/rediacc/)
    • repositories/ — encrypted LUKS images (one per repo GUID)
    • mounts/ — decrypted mount points (accessible when repo is mounted)
    • immovable/ — per-repo Docker daemon data
    • Datastore is a BTRFS pool file on the system disk. Effective free space = min(disk free, datastore free). Expand with: rdc datastore resize

repo.keyConcepts:
Key Concepts:

  Compose & Rediaccfile
    • renet compose -- up -d (never raw docker compose). The -- separator is required
    • Rediaccfile must define up() and down() functions. up() should: create dirs, generate configs, start containers
    • compose ports: are ignored (network_mode:host). Use rediacc.service_port label for external access
    • restart: always/unless-stopped are auto-stripped by renet and saved to .rediacc.json — the router watchdog auto-recovers stopped services
    • Each service gets a loopback IP. eBPF bind rewriting handles isolation transparently, so apps can bind to 0.0.0.0
    • To connect to sibling services use their service name (e.g. "db", "redis") — renet injects all service names as hostnames. Never embed ${DB_IP} in connection strings stored inside databases — it bakes the IP and breaks fork isolation (validation error)
    • Health checks can use localhost. Example: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8080/health"]

  Storage
    • Bind-mount to ${REDIACC_WORKING_DIR}/data, ${REDIACC_WORKING_DIR}/config, etc.
    • Example: volumes: ['${REDIACC_WORKING_DIR}/data:/var/lib/postgresql/data']
    • Docker named volumes are excluded from forks and backups
    • Config files bind-mounted into containers must be world-readable (644) if the container runs as a non-default UID

  Routing
    • Grand repo auto-route: https://{service}.{repo}.{machine}.{baseDomain} (wildcard cert *.{repo}.{machine}.{baseDomain} auto-provisioned by Traefik on first repo up)
    • Fork auto-route: https://{service}-fork-{tag}.{repo}.{machine}.{baseDomain} (uses parent repo's wildcard cert, zero rate limit impact)
    • Custom domain: traefik.enable=true + traefik.http.routers.{name}.rule=Host(`domain.com`)
    • TCP/UDP forwarding: rediacc.tcp_ports=5432 / rediacc.udp_ports=53
    • Custom domains (rediacc.domain label) are ignored on forks — the domain belongs to the grand repo

  Lifecycle
    • repo delete fully cleans up: storage, Docker daemon, loopback IPs, systemd units
    • repo down stops containers but keeps Docker daemon and IPs (quick restart with repo up)
    • depends_on with condition: service_healthy handles startup order but not runtime recovery
    • If a database stops cleanly (exit 0), dependent services crash-loop. Fix: rdc repo up <repo-ref>
    • Autostart: rdc repo admin autostart enable <repo-ref> — auto-mounts and starts repo on machine boot
    • Scheduled backups skip fork repos automatically. Use rdc repo push <repo-ref> --to <remote> for manual fork backup
    • rdc repo promote <fork-ref> — replace production data with fork data (preserves identity). Revert with: rdc repo promote <backup-fork-ref>

  Naming & targeting
    • Grand (production) repo: reference it as <repo>, equivalently <repo>:latest (latest is the default tag). A bare ref resolves to the exact config key, else falls back to <repo>:latest.
    • Fork: always <repo>:<tag> with a non-latest tag (e.g. app:test). up/down/delete/term/sync all take the same <repo>:<tag>.
    • So `app` targets the GRAND; `app:test` targets that FORK. Always include the tag when acting on a fork — the one ambiguous case is a fork mistakenly registered under the bare/latest name.
    • Agents may only modify forks; grand repos are protected (override only via REDIACC_ALLOW_GRAND_REPO, which must be set by the operator before the session). Forks are the safe, disposable unit.

term.repoContextRequired:
Command requires repository context.

Detected "{{detected}}" which needs DOCKER_HOST and repository environment variables.
These are only available when the target is a repository.

Instead of:
  rdc term connect {{machine}} -c "{{command}}"

Use:
  rdc term connect <repo-ref> -c "{{command}}"
term.dockerComposeForbidden:
"docker compose" is not permitted in repository context.

Use "renet compose -- <args>" instead so per-repo loopback IPs, host network injection, CRIU capabilities, and compose validation are applied. Running "docker compose" directly bypasses all of this and silently corrupts the deployment.

For orchestrated deploys, prefer: rdc repo up <repo-ref>
term.fileWriteDetected:
File write detected ({{detected}}). Use rdc repo sync instead:
  rdc repo sync upload <repo-ref> --local FILE --remote PATH

rsync transfers files with delta compression, checksums, and proper permissions.

overview.heading: Overview
overview.text: The **Rediacc CLI** (`rdc`) is a command-line interface for managing self-hosted infrastructure — machines, repositories, storage, backups, and more.

installation.heading: Installation
installation.text: Download the latest binary for your platform from the [Rediacc releases page](https://www.rediacc.com) or install via your package manager:

errors.intro: When something goes wrong, the CLI provides clear error messages:

meanings.noActiveConfig: No config is active — create one with `rdc config init`
meanings.permissionDenied: Your account lacks the required permissions
meanings.machineRequired: Specify a machine with `--machine` or set a config default
meanings.teamRequired: Specify a team with `--team` or set a config default
meanings.regionRequired: Specify a region with `--region` or set a config default

outputFormats.heading: Output Formats
outputFormats.text: All list/get commands support multiple output formats via `--output`:
outputFormats.closing: This makes it easy to integrate Rediacc CLI into scripts, CI/CD pipelines, and automation workflows.

config.afterDescription: Config files store connection details (API URL, credentials, default team/region/bridge) so you can switch between environments quickly.

health.afterDescription: The health command outputs system metrics, container status, service stability, and storage information — useful for CI/CD pipeline checks.
